title: feat(remote): weight S3 permits by pack size so large restores can't saturate the pool

labels.name: area:daemon
labels.description: Background daemon: IPC, prefetch coordination, concurrency

labels.name: area:remote
labels.description: S3 sync, planner, the untrusted-remote trust boundary

body:
## Status

Most of this issue landed in #719 (c3bac93). One item is left, so the scope below is trimmed to it.

## Remaining work: weighted permits

Every S3 operation acquires exactly one permit from `s3_semaphore` regardless of how much it transfers. The pool is built as `Semaphore::new(config.s3_concurrency)` (`src/daemon.rs:2376`) and every acquisition site calls `.acquire()` rather than `acquire_many` (2569, 2660, 2727, 3454, 3528, 3889, 4046, 4275, 4325, 4732, 4932, 6816, 6999; line refs as of v0.19.0).

A pool sized for N concurrent operations therefore admits N large pack restores at once. Permits should scale with pack size, capped so that one pack can never require more than the pool holds and deadlock against itself.

### Acceptance criteria

- A restore acquires permits proportional to its expected pack size, capped strictly below the pool size.
- A pack above the cap still runs, holding the capped number of permits rather than waiting forever.
- Small operations (HEAD, key-cache LIST) keep taking a single permit and are not starved behind one large restore.
- The existing `available_permits` accounting test is extended rather than replaced.

## Landed in #719

- Error classification into `{Miss, Transient, Timeout}`, with exponential backoff and per-attempt jitter (`src/remote_resilience.rs`).
- `RemoteBreaker`, generalizing `RemoteHealth` to every remote op: HEAD, GET, PUT, and key-cache LIST all feed it and consult it. While degraded a restore answers miss immediately and rustc recompiles locally.
- Deadline-bounded restore via `remote_restore_timeout_secs`.
- `KeyedSingleflight`, the named per-key lock that replaced the busy-poll download dedup.
- `NegativeKeyCache`, the persistent negative-lookup cache, which also closed #564.

## Out of scope

A detached signature binding a cache key to its manifest, tracked separately in #179 as a distinct trust layer.
